prompt: Produce a formatted price line with printf: a left-justified 10-character name column and a right-justified 6-character price with two decimals. Complete the printPrice method.
explanation: printf format specifiers pack alignment, width, and precision into one string: %-10s left-justifies a string in a 10-character field (the minus flag means left), and %6.2f right-justifies a number in 6 characters with exactly 2 digits after the decimal point, padding with spaces. %n emits the platform line separator, which the tests normalize to \n before comparing. Values wider than the field (a long name or a big price) are never truncated -- the field simply grows.
hints: The whole method is a single System.out.printf call using the format string from the task description.
%-10s means: string, minimum 10 characters, and the '-' flag left-justifies it (pads on the right).
%6.2f means: floating point, at least 6 characters total, exactly 2 after the decimal point, padded with spaces on the left; end the format with %n for the newline.
